description.narrative: The Joint Devolution support programme is anticipated to start with an inception phase, approx. 4-6 months. A comprehensive county assessment of governance structures as well as public service delivery, structures, and performance, will be the main activity during this period. The assessment will be conducted in the 8 targeted counties through a Request for proposal (RFP) to secure an internationally recognized firm with a mixture of international decentralization/public sector (service delivery) experts and national experts. The assessments are anticipated to start1 September and the reports to be finalized 31 January 2025. The recruitment of the firm will follow UNDPs policies and procedures for procurement of firms,1 UN Women and Unicef will be part of the evaluation of the bids as well as providing input to the RFP.The joint devolution programme team have designed and developed the Joint devolution support programme document as a joint team. All interactions with donors have emphasized that resources are being mobilized to the joint programme, not to one of the participating UN agencies. The programme document has not used already existing programmes or projects funding agreements to indicate that financial resources have been put in the joint programme. The full programme document has an Annex which describes programmes and projects the agencies currently are implementing that are of relevance for the joint programme.

condition.narrative: The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
